title: WITH clause within EA Sparx query
body:
Is it possible to use WITH clauses within an EA Sparx query ?

I wrote this one :

with Activities as

    (
    select t_connector.start_object_id as Object2_id, t_object.* from t_object 
        join t_connector on t_connector.end_object_id=t_object.Object_id
        where t_object.Object_type= 'Activity'

    union

    select t_connector.end_object_id as Object2_id, t_object.*  from t_object  
        join t_connector on t_connector.start_object_id=t_object.Object_id
        where t_object.Object_type= 'Activity'

    )

select * from

    (
    select obj.object_id, count(other.object_id) as 'Activities' from
        t_object obj left join Activities as other on obj.Object_id=other.Object2_id

    group by obj.object_id
    ) as ac 

where object_id in (143306, 143321, 143226, 143326)

and it doesn't return any rows nor throw any errors, while the same query with the WITH-statement placed inline returns the expected results:

select * from
    (
    select obj.object_id, count(other.object_id) as 'Activities' from
        t_object obj left join 
            (
            select t_connector.start_object_id as Object2_id, t_object.* from t_object 
                join t_connector on t_connector.end_object_id=t_object.Object_id
                where t_object.Object_type= 'Activity'

            union

            select t_connector.end_object_id as Object2_id, t_object.*  from t_object  
                join t_connector on t_connector.start_object_id=t_object.Object_id
                where t_object.Object_type= 'Activity'

            )
        as other on obj.Object_id=other.Object2_id

    group by obj.object_id
    ) as ac 

where object_id in (143306, 143321, 143226, 143326)

I know that the SQL engine of EA is a bit tricky (e.g. the query cannot start by a comment).

Is there some tricks here to let WITH clauses working in EA ?

title: GPU Runtime Error when memory is available
body:
I'm currently training some neural network models and I've found that for some reason the model will sometimes fail before ~200 iterations due to a runtime error, despite there being memory available. The error is:

RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 MiB (GPU 0; 10.76 GiB total capacity; 1.79 GiB already allocated; 3.44 MiB free; 9.76 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

Which shows how only ~1.8GB of RAM is being used when there should be 9.76GB available.

I have found that when I find a good seed (just by random searching), and the model gets past the first few hundred iterations, it will generally run fine afterwards. It seems as though the model doesn't have as much memory available very early on in training, but I don't know how to solve this.

title: Adehabitaths compana() function freezing with 0's in availability matrix
body:
I am trying to run compana() from the adehabitatHS package, but whenever there is a 0 in the availability matrix, the function hangs and I have to kill R using Task Manager.

I created a small dummy matrix to test this and reproduced the issue. The availability matrix containing zeros does not run, but replacing all zeros with a positive number does.

The package documentation states that compana() should handle zeros in the availability matrix:

"When zero values are found in the matrix of available habitats, the function compana uses the procedure termed 'weighted mean lambda' described in Aebischer et al. (1993: Appendix 2), instead of the usual lambda (see examples). Zero values can be found in the matrix of available habitats when the third-order habitat selection is under focus. In this case, it may occur that some habitat types are available to some animals and not to the others."

Am I missing something? I have considered adding a small constant (e.g., 0.0001) to the availability matrix in my actual data, as I have heard others do, but that seems like it could strongly affect the results mathematically. Is it not as problematic as I think?

Any help would be appreciated.

R code for small matrix test:

use <- matrix(c(10,16,30,0,0,5,0,3,0,7,0,0), nrow = 3,ncol=4, byrow=TRUE)
availability <- matrix(c(27,89,31,0,0,67,0,90,2,18,1,31), nrow = 3, ncol=4,byrow=TRUE) # availability matrix with 0's in it

#I understand this dummy matrix has its own issues (having more habitats than animals), but this is just to demonstrate the problem with 0's in the availability matrix.

use_percent <- (use / rowSums(use)) *100
availability_percent <- (availability / rowSums(availability)) *100
test <-compana(use_percent, availability_percent, test = c("randomisation"), rnv = 0.0001, nrep = 500, alpha = 0.1) #causes R to freeze
availability <- matrix(c(27,89,31,12,3,67,9,90,2,18,1,31), nrow = 3, ncol=4,byrow=TRUE) #changing all 0's to be >0
availability_percent <- (availability / rowSums(availability)) *100

test2 <-compana(use_percent, availability_percent, test = c("randomisation"), rnv = 0.0001, nrep = 500, alpha = 0.1) # this runs just fine

This does not delete the version 3. https://docs.delta.io/0.4.0/delta-update.html says

"delete removes the data from the latest version of the Delta table but does not remove it from the physical storage until the old versions are explicitly vacuumed"

If i have to run vacuum command how to use them on latest dates and not older dates.

title: Frequency/histogram of an array
body:
Searching for a way to transform an array to object of key-value pairs representing individual elements and the number of occurrences.

Similar to LIST_HISTOGRAM function:

SELECT LIST_HISTOGRAM(['a','b','d','d','a','a']);
-- {a=3, b=1, d=2}

db<>fiddle demo

Input:

CREATE TABLE tab(arr ARRAY) AS
SELECT ['x','x','z'] UNION SELECT ['a','b','d','d','a','a'];

Desired output:

input result
["x","x","z"] {"x": 2, "z": 1}
["a","b","d","d","a","a"] { "a": 3, "b": 1,"d": 2}

Searching for inline, SQL-first approach.

I would like to avoid flattening, transforming, and aggregating back:

WITH cte AS (
    SELECT tab.arr, s.value::TEXT AS v, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM tab,LATERAL FLATTEN(tab.arr) AS s
    GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT arr, OBJECT_AGG(v, cnt)
FROM cte
GROUP BY ALL;

title: Why do some package install methods fail due to dependencies while other install methods work?
body:
I am looking for some insight into some of the errors I received while trying to install packages. I would like to know why they occurred, why the solutions I came to worked, and what I can do to avoid this going forward.

I was seeing an error when trying to install tmap with the following:

remotes::install_github("r-tmap/tmap")

I was having issues with dependent packages (xfun, digest, yaml etc.) as shown below:

Warning: cannot remove prior installation of package ‘yaml’
Warning in file.copy(savedcopy, lib, recursive = TRUE) :
  problem copying C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\R\win-
library\4.3\00LOCK\yaml\libs\x64\yaml.dll to C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\R\win-
library\4.3\yaml\libs\x64\yaml.dll: Permission denied
Warning: restored ‘yaml’

Why this would be the case with some file updates and not others? I am unfamiliar with this 00LOCK in the path name, so wondering why that surfaces sometimes?

The solution for this was uninstalling them and deleting all the files manually from the package library.

After resolving that, I reran the tmap install. Many dependencies were installed with most successfully installing (rmarkdown, tinytex, knitr etc.):

* installing *source* package 'tinytex' ...
** package 'tinytex' successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
** using staged installation
** R

** help
*** installing help indices

** testing if installed package can be loaded from temporary location
** testing if installed package can be loaded from final location

* DONE (tinytex)

However, I had an issue solely with servr:

* installing *source* package 'servr' ...

** using staged installation

Error in loadNamespace(j <- i[[1L]], c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[j]]) :

I solved this by installing servr through the package manager in RStudio. It only worked when I selected 'Yes' for compiling from source packages.

Why am I getting those permission denied errors? I don't understand why servr and the version of xfun (?) were an issue from the tmap dependency install when it worked perfectly when I installed servr separately.

title: Why is Dapper failing to substitute a parameter in a SQL statement
body:
I have the following method in my code to query a table with an encrypted column in SQL Server.

public async Task<ConnectionDetails?> LoadConnectionDetailsBy(string systemId, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    ConnectionDetails? details = null;

    using (var connection = new SqlConnection(_connectionString))
    {
        await connection.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);

        var sql = """
            open symmetric key ConnectionDetailsSymmetricKey
            decryption by asymmetric key GeneralAsymmetricKey
            with password = @encryptionKey
            """;

        await connection.ExecuteAsync(sql, new { encryptionKey = _encryptionKey });

        try
        {
            sql = """
            select
                SystemId,
                convert([nvarchar](max), decryptbykey([EncryptedConnectionString])) as ConnectionString
            from ConnectionDetails
            where SystemId = @systemId
            """;

            details = await connection.QuerySingleOrDefaultAsync<ConnectionDetails>(sql, new { systemId });
        }
        finally
        {
            sql = "close symmetric key ConnectionDetailsSymmetricKey";
            await connection.ExecuteAsync(sql);
        }
    }

    return details;
}

The problem I have is the first SQL statement executed to open the key fails with an error:

Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.SqlException: Incorrect syntax near '@encryptionKey'

I cannot see why this should fail. If I paste in the password directly it works as expected. What mistake have I made here?
